# Independent audit of the planar dominated-centroid dual certificate

Audited source:
`candidate abf220aa65271e88`.
Result: PASS for its ordinary density theorem and stated identical-endpoint
application. The archived dominated midpoint coupling also gives the
arbitrary equal-volume endpoint extension described below.

## Ordinary proof

After |K|=1, eta domination gives 0<=alpha<=1 and absolute continuity.
The centroid of 1_K dx+2eta lies in int K: every supporting functional
has a strict average gap, since 1_K dx has positive full-dimensional
mass. Thus the source cap fraction s is in (0,1), so every division is
legitimate.

For the scalar projection, cap-root concavity follows by the actual
Minkowski inclusion of upper caps. The projection density is positive
and continuous on its open interval. Consequently the upper-tail value
V(X) is uniform on (0,1). Pushing eta forward preserves domination by
that uniform law, hence produces a density h in [0,1]. Jensen has the
correct direction: concavity yields G(E_rho X)>=E_rho G(X).

The two left-filled intervals minimizing the integral of sqrt(v) have
lengths r and alpha-r and are feasible because eta<=1_K dx. Their
integrals give exactly the source formula(2). With
U=1/s, E=r/s, Q=(s+alpha-r)/s, division by s^(3/2) gives

    phi(U)+2phi(Q)+2phi(E)>=2/3,
    phi(t)=t-(2/3)t^(3/2).

The domain U,Q>=1, E in[0,1] is correct. The additional actual condition
Q<=U is not used, which only weakens the relaxation.

For b=1+a>=0 the dual inequality has the exact nonnegative factorization

    b^3/3-phi(t)-a t
      =(sqrt(t)-b)^2(2sqrt(t)+b)/3.

The a<=-1 case follows immediately from phi(t)+a t<=0. The chosen values
are b=3/2 and b=9/16. With multiplicities 1,2,2 their sum is
7155/2048. Combining with the scalar lower bound gives
D=U+2Q-7E/4<=17369/3072. The mass ratio is exactly

    (1+2alpha)/(s+r)=(U+2Q+2E-2)/(1+E).

The resulting upper bound
[11225/3072+(15/4)E]/(1+E) increases on[0,1], because its numerator
slope exceeds its constant term. Its endpoint is 22745/6144. Thus the
claimed constant c_*=6144/22745 is established without any unstated
shape restriction on eta. Its gap from 4/15 is positive, with
6144*15-4*22745=1180.

All halfplane boundaries are null for both measures. Parallel translation
to the centroid only reduces the captured mass, so the closed-containing
halfplanes are all covered.

## Coupling extension to different equal-volume endpoints

The archived theorem `candidate 71bcdfc8eb8340c6`
provides eta of mass v with eta<=1_K dx whenever |A|=|B|=v and
(A+B)/2 subset K. It has centroid (g_A+g_B)/2, and for every compatible
closed ambient cap,

    eta(H_0)<=|A intersect H_-1|+|B intersect H_1|.

A direct convex-body proof requiring only conditional one-dimensional
substitution is also saved in
`accepted fact 486fe778f838d99d,f6641f09c19819a3`.

Consequently g=centroid(1_K dx+2eta) is the continuous coordinate of the
actual three-fiber mixed centroid. It belongs to K, and for every closed
ambient halfspace containing (0,g), the actual captured mass is at least

    c_* (|K|+2v).

The purely integer halfspaces contain K and one endpoint, and trivially
satisfy the same bound. Arbitrary normals are handled by the affine-offset
coupling inequality. This is a deterministic centroid conclusion, not
an expectation over candidate centers.

If k=|K|/v, Brunn–Minkowski gives k>=1. The edge comparison

    c_*(k+2)>(k+1)/3

holds exactly for k<14119/4313, and hence throughout[1,3]. At k=3 the
strict gap is1180/68235. No upper ratio restriction is needed for the
c_* total-mass bound itself. This still does not handle unequal endpoint
volumes or a noninteger mixed centroid.
